prompt: Take apart a raw HTTP response string into its status code, its headers (with lowercased keys) and its body. Complete the three methods in HttpResponseParser, then run the tests.
explanation:
A response is one block of text with a fixed shape: a status line, header lines, one blank line, then the body. Splitting on 
 gives you the lines; the status code is the second word of the first line, and each header splits at its FIRST colon so that values containing colons survive intact. Lowercasing the keys makes lookups predictable, because HTTP header names are case-insensitive on the wire. indexOf("

") finds the header/body boundary in one step.
hints: raw.split("\r\n", -1) turns the whole response into lines; index 0 is the status line and the header lines follow it.
Use line.indexOf(':') and substring() rather than split(":") -- a value like a URL can contain colons of its own.
For the body, find the index of "\r\n\r\n" and take substring(index + 4); return "" when that marker is missing.
